title: Not Our Water
description: A water main blew on Delphine Street at four o'clock and the block is filling up. Ronnie gets the three people who could fix it on one call, and every one of them swears the flood belongs to one of the others. Meanwhile a homeowner narrates his rising basement live.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM. There is water coming up out of Delphine Street, a lot of it, and tonight we've got the three people who can sort this out, all on one line. Patricia from the Water Authority, Darnell with the road crew, and Winston from the city. Welcome, folks.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Quick question before we start. Is the valve off?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: We'll get to the valve, Barry. Patricia, you're closest to this. What's the situation?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia-utility
lines.text: Well, Ronnie, I've pulled the schematic, and I want to be very clear. <p:0.3> That line on Delphine was decommissioned. Retired in oh-nine. So whatever's coming up out of there, per the schematic, it is not our water.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's not your water.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia-utility
lines.text: It can't be. The pipe's retired, Barry. A retired pipe doesn't carry water. That's just how it works.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now that's fair. Darnell, your crew was out there this morning, weren't you?

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: We were digging there, yeah, but I'll stop you right now, Ronnie. We marked it. We marked every line on that block. And the pipe we hit? <p:0.3> That's not the one we hit.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: That's... that's not the one you hit. But you hit a pipe.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: We hit a different pipe, Barry. A dry one. We marked it. The wet one, the one doing all this? Different pipe entirely. Not ours.

lines.speaker: caller-steve
lines.text: Uh, hi, yeah, Ronnie? It's Steve, on Delphine. <p:0.3> I'm in my basement. We are at the bottom step now. Just the one step covered. Over.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Thanks for the update, Steve, hang in there. Winston, you're the city's Underground Assets man. This is your wheelhouse.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: It is precisely NOT my wheelhouse, Ronnie, and I'll thank you to be accurate. <p:0.3> I oversee underground assets. Conduits, vaults, fiber. A burst main? That falls outside my asset class. Wholly outside it.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: So it's not your water either.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: I don't do water, Barry. I do assets. Water is, frankly, beneath my department. Literally and otherwise.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Okay but somebody's water is in Steve's basement. Is the valve off?

lines.speaker: caller-patricia-utility
lines.text: There's no valve to shut off, Barry, because the line is decommissioned. You can't shut a valve on a pipe that isn't ours.

lines.speaker: caller-steve
lines.text: Third stair, Ronnie. We're at the third stair. <p:0.3> The Christmas decorations are floating. Over.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Noted, Steve. Darnell, if Patricia's pipe is retired, then the wet pipe must be the one your crew was near.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Near is not the same as hit, Ronnie. We were near a lot of pipes. We marked all of 'em. The one that's gushing, I'm telling you, that's not the one we hit.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: And whatever it is, it's flowing, which makes it surface conduct, which makes it not mine. I catalogue assets at rest. Moving water is somebody else's category.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It is RISING in a man's house, Winston!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Rising! Then it's gaining elevation, Barry, which is its own asset class, which is, again, not mine.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia-utility
lines.text: Per the schematic, that water predates our jurisdiction. It was retired in oh-nine. It's grandfathered. It's nobody's at this point, honestly.

lines.speaker: caller-steve
lines.text: Sixth stair. The freezer just tipped over. <p:0.3> There's a lasagna doing laps. Over.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Steve, that's a real shame about the lasagna. Folks, can we agree somebody go turn the water off?

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Can't turn off water that isn't ours, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia-utility
lines.text: Decommissioned!

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Different pipe!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Outside my asset class!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: IS THE VALVE OFF?!

lines.speaker: caller-patricia-utility
lines.text: Not ours!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Not mine!

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Not the one we hit!

lines.speaker: caller-steve
lines.text: Top stair, Ronnie. <p:0.3> It's at the top stair. It's at the phone. <p:0.4> ...You know what? Now that it's up here, getting a good look at it... <p:0.3> this isn't even my water.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Steve? <p:0.3> Steve, you're cutting out.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Well, folks, the good news is, by unanimous agreement, that is nobody's water. <p:0.3> Delphine Street, you're free to keep it. We'll be right back.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: The valve was never off, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now that's fair. <p:0.3> Is it heading our way?

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's downhill to us, Ronnie. <p:0.3> There's a river in our parking lot.
